objectives: Consolidate /r/ sound recognition, decoding, encoding, comprehension and fluency.
Check connected-reading accuracy, smoothness and appropriate pacing.
Route learners to targeted remediation when a critical component remains below target.
concepts: Fluency depends on accurate decoding and repeated connected reading.
A diagnostic samples several related skills to locate instructional needs.
Accuracy must be protected while fluency develops.

definitions.definition: Accurate, appropriately paced and increasingly automatic reading.
An assessment used to identify current strengths and instructional needs.
A distinct skill area measured within a broader phonics outcome.

workedExamples: Decoding: read unfamiliar taught /r/ CVC words.
Comprehension: answer questions from controlled text.
Fluency: reread controlled text accurately and smoothly.
commonMistakes: Treating speed as more important than accuracy.
Advancing despite a critical weak component.
Guessing unknown words instead of decoding them.

basic: Review each /r/ component with short controlled tasks.
conceptual: Match observed errors to the correct diagnostic component.
application: Interpret sample diagnostic results and choose an evidence-based support route.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why accurate connected reading matters when developing fluency.
mixedReview: Combine /r/ recognition, CVC decoding, spelling, comprehension and fluency.

mistakeBasedRevision: If fluency is low, check decoding accuracy before increasing reading speed.
weakTopicRevision: Revisit the lowest-performing component with targeted practice.

scoring.method: component-level accuracy with overall mastery gate

routingRules.atOrAboveMastery: Advance to the next consolidation/reassessment stage when overall mastery is at least 0.8 and no critical component is below target.
routingRules.belowMastery: Route to targeted remediation for the weakest component before reassessment.

outcomes: Learner receives evidence-based routing for remediation or progression.

questions.question: In “Rin has a red rag,” who has the rag?
In “The rat is on the rug,” where is the rat?
What happens first in “Rin gets a red rag. Rin puts it on the rug.”?
options: Rin puts it on the rug.

questions.question: Which word belongs to the -ug family?
A learner decodes /r/ words accurately but reads a controlled passage with many pauses. Which component needs support?
A learner reads /r/ words accurately but cannot explain what happened in a short passage. Which component needs support?
Why should fluency be checked together with accuracy?
options: A fast reading with errors does not show secure reading.
Speed always matters more than accuracy.
Accuracy can be ignored during reading.

questions.question: A learner makes several decoding errors while reading a controlled /r/ passage. What is the best diagnostic response?
options: Record the decoding weakness and route targeted practice before judging fluency.
Tell the learner to read faster.
Ignore the errors and score only speed.

questions.question: If the learner reaches the mastery target and has no critical component below target, what is the appropriate next step?
options: Advance to the next consolidation/reassessment stage.
